paths.description: Homepage and global template. Covers first-view hierarchy, preferences, mobile reflow, performance, security, privacy, discoverability, accessibility, and memory.
Tamil 2026 listing template. Covers catalog navigation, pagination, dense links, and category browsing.
Representative primary journey: listing to movie detail to format choice to final named download link. Covers content detail and flow continuity; the binary itself was not downloaded.
Movie request form template. Covers labels, native controls, invalid submission, focus, and error handling.
Unknown URL. Covers HTTP/not-found recovery and misleading success states.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to light mode; the probe reports body background rgb(249,249,249), text rgb(0,0,0), and colorScheme normal while the emulated dark preference is active.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define paired surface, text, border, and link colors with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query.

findings.summary: Multi-page navigation swaps abruptly without cross-document View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM and CSS inspection across listing, detail, and format pages found no @view-transition rule or authored view-transition-name; navigation is a full abrupt document swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared header and title elements, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Deep pages lack orientation cues and meaningful current-location navigation.
findings.evidence: The listing and detail screenshots show no breadcrumbs, current category marker, or back-to-results control; every page repeats a large A-Z block and a generic home footer.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic breadcrumbs and a visible current-location state, retain a clear back-to-results path, and use directional transition cues where appropriate.

findings.summary: Repeated promotional and keyword-heavy blocks crowd out the catalog content.
findings.evidence: The mobile first viewport gives most space to repeated branding, a broken Telegram promotion, and search; detail pages then repeat A-Z categories and incoming-search-term keyword blocks around a single useful link.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the primary catalog or download action into the first useful viewport, remove repeated keyword blocks, and collapse secondary A-Z navigation behind a compact disclosure.

findings.summary: Many primary links have undersized touch targets and the search input removes visible focus.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe measured repeated Download links at only 17px high; the search input computed outline is none with no box-shadow after focus. Lighthouse also identified interaction accessibility failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Give links and controls at least a 44px touch area and add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline that is not removed from the search input.

findings.summary: The first viewport obscures the catalog’s primary task behind branding and generic promotion.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot contains branding, a non-working Telegram link, repeated domain text, and search before any movie/category choice. The useful catalog begins below the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: State the catalog purpose once, surface recent movies and browse categories immediately, and remove or repair competing promotional actions.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs silently show a generic menu instead of an honest 404 and recovery state.
findings.evidence: The unknown-route probe shows a normal Moviesda title and category menu with no 404 heading, explanation, or retry/back guidance; the page gives no indication that the requested content was not found.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 404, show a clear not-found heading, preserve the requested context, and offer search, recent content, and a home/back recovery action.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP misses the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 4.0s and FCP at 2.6s, while the direct trace under an unthrottled condition measured LCP at 951ms. The throttled result identifies a real slow-network/mobile risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize first-view content, remove the render-blocking font import, and defer non-essential third-party scripts until after consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript and a font stylesheet dominate a very small page load.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 208,156 transferred bytes, of which 192,140 are third-party; Google Tag Manager alone is 166,672 bytes. Lighthouse reports render-blocking requests with about 1.8s potential savings and 68KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the unknown ad script, gate analytics behind consent, load analytics after the primary content, and self-host or replace the render-blocking font with a system stack.

findings.summary: Text and links fail minimum color contrast and links rely on color alone.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed color-contrast and link-in-text-block. The screenshots show low-contrast orange and pink text on pale backgrounds and many links distinguished only by color.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose tokenized foreground/background pairs meeting WCAG AA and underline inline links instead of relying on color alone.

findings.summary: Some visible control labels do not match their accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed label-content-name-mismatch. The visible search button says “🔍 Search Movie” while aria-label replaces that with “Submit search”.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the accessible name contain the visible label, for example aria-label="Search movies", or remove the redundant aria-label when button text is sufficient.

findings.summary: Visual section titles are frequently non-heading divs and keyboard focus is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Listing and detail DOM use div.line for page titles instead of headings; the platform probe found the search input suppresses its outline while surrounding controls use browser outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a single h1 for each page title, preserve logical heading levels, and define a consistent visible :focus-visible treatment for every interactive element.

findings.summary: Repeated link targets are too short for comfortable touch use.
findings.evidence: Although mobile reflow has no horizontal overflow, the target probe measured many catalog/download links at 17px high, well below a comfortable 44px target.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase row and inline-link hit areas with block links or padding while preserving reflow and user zoom.

findings.summary: A third-party script fails during load and DevTools records issues.
findings.evidence: The HAR records xm.viragocosech.com failing with net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB, and Lighthouse reports Inspector Issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the failing unknown-origin script or serve a valid, correctly typed resource from a trusted origin; verify a clean console and Issues panel.

findings.summary: Every folder image omits intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 22 of 22 images without width and height attributes. They are one reused SVG displayed at 15px, so transfer cost is small but intrinsic sizing is not explicit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width="15" height="15" to folder images, use empty alt when decorative, and keep CSS sizing consistent.

findings.summary: The page is not eligible for BFCache and triggers browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons and a failing Inspector Issues audit; the HAR also shows an ORB-blocked third-party script.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect and remove the reported BFCache blockers, eliminate the failing third-party request, and retest page restoration and the DevTools Issues panel.

findings.summary: Prominent navigation includes crawlable-looking links that lead nowhere or to the wrong page.
findings.evidence: The Telegram link resolves to the current page hash and the footer Disclaimer link resolves to home. Listing pagination also uses href="#" for the active page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the real Telegram and disclaimer URLs, render the current pagination item as text with aria-current="page", and reserve anchors for actual destinations.

findings.summary: Public pages omit canonical links despite many similar routes and parameterized pagination.
findings.evidence: The platform probe reports canonical null; inspected homepage, listing, detail, and form heads contain no rel=canonical while sitemap and index directives are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a self-referencing canonical URL per indexable page and canonicalize pagination and alternate route variants consistently with the sitemap.

findings.summary: Movie pages lack structured entity data and complete social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero JSON-LD blocks; page heads have Open Graph title, description, URL, and type but no og:image. Detail content therefore exposes no Movie schema or preview image.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Movie JSON-LD matching visible content and complete Open Graph/Twitter preview fields including an image.

findings.summary: Session and analytics cookies are insecure and the site lacks baseline security headers.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All four cookies lack Secure; PHPSESSID also lacks HttpOnly and all report SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite value on PHPSESSID; secure analytics cookies; deploy HSTS, CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and an opaque ad script load before any consent or user action.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence identifies Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics plus xm.viragocosech.com; HAR shows five third-party origins and 192,140 third-party bytes, while no consent UI appears on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the opaque third-party script, document the analytics purpose, minimize collected fields, and load non-essential analytics only after valid consent where required.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no HSTS, clickjacking defense, CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or nosniff header.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and an explicit least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The not-found state is indistinguishable from a successful catalog page.
findings.evidence: The unknown route renders a normal menu and title with no failure message or recovery explanation, creating a misleading success state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return and render an explicit 404 state with useful recovery actions, and apply the same clear-state pattern to network and server failures.

findings.summary: The stylesheet is not prepared for bidirectional or translated layouts.
findings.evidence: HTML declares lang=en, but inspected CSS repeatedly uses physical left/right properties such as text-align:left, margin-right, padding-left, and border-left instead of logical inline/block equivalents.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep accurate page language, add dir when needed, and replace physical layout properties with margin-inline, padding-inline, border-inline-start, and text-align:start.

findings.summary: Prominent and legal-looking navigation is misleading.
findings.evidence: “Join our Telegram Channel” is a prominent link to # rather than a channel, while “Disclaimer” links to the homepage. These controls promise destinations they do not provide.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove claims that cannot be fulfilled and link each labeled action to its stated destination; provide a real disclaimer page and accurate ownership/contact information.

findings.summary: Search and request inputs omit input-assistance metadata.
findings.evidence: The request invalid-state probe reports an empty autocomplete value, and inspected search/request controls do not declare useful autocomplete or input-purpose tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Add appropriate autocomplete and inputmode tokens, and set autocomplete="off" only where a field genuinely has no reusable user data.

findings.summary: Background analytics and an opaque script outweigh the site’s own page resources.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 192,140 of 208,156 transferred bytes are third-party, including 166,672 bytes of Google Tag Manager and a failed opaque ad-script request.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the failed third-party script and defer or eliminate analytics so background work is proportionate to the simple static catalog.

findings.summary: Third-party resources consume over 92% of transferred bytes without visible user value.
findings.evidence: HAR records 192,140 third-party bytes out of 208,156 total and five third-party origins; there is no user-visible media that justifies this budget.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte/origin budget, remove opaque vendors, and load analytics only when its value and consent justify the cost.

taskList.title: Secure headers, session cookies, and defensive browser policies
Remove opaque third-party code and gate/minimize analytics
Fix contrast, semantic headings, focus visibility, names, and touch targets
Put catalog actions first and remove repetitive keyword chrome
Repair misleading Telegram and disclaimer links
Add canonical and structured social/entity metadata
Add dark mode and cross-document transition support
Add intrinsic image dimensions and input assistance metadata
Use logical CSS properties and clearer deep-page orientation
